body:
Your team is counting down to annual leave. You are counting the things you meant to organise in March. Somewhere between the budget spreadsheet and the Christmas party booking, “refresh the office” is still sitting on the list.

For business owners, directors and office managers, the Christmas shutdown can be a useful opportunity to update a workplace while fewer people are using it. The aim: less disruption to the working day and a refreshed space ready for the New Year.

The catch? Your office may be winding down, but the supplier order books are doing the opposite.

## The office is going on holiday. The to-do list apparently isn't.

If new workstations, a better meeting room, tired reception furniture or an office refurbishment is on your radar, now is the time to turn the idea into a conversation.

Work during a planned shutdown can reduce the need to move people around desks, interrupt meetings or work around a full office. It can also provide a clearer window for furniture installation, agreed refurbishment works and a thorough clean before staff return.

That is an opportunity to reduce disruption, rather than a promise of zero downtime. Building access, supplier closures, trade availability, IT requirements and the actual scope still need to line up. A quieter office is helpful; a locked loading dock is less festive.

## Custom furniture: the calendar has entered the chat

Custom and made-to-order furniture needs decisions before manufacture: dimensions, finishes, drawings where required, approvals and an accepted order. Christmas production cut-offs can arrive well before the office Christmas party.

Supplier books can start closing to pre-Christmas work in the coming weeks, and some products may already need a New Year delivery plan. There is no single industry-wide cut-off: we need to check the actual manufacturer, product and finish before confirming a date.

If custom furniture is part of your plan, speak with us now. An inspiration folder is a great start. It does not, unfortunately, reserve a place in the factory queue.

[Compare standard, modified and custom office furniture](/blog/standard-modified-custom-office-furniture-newcastle)

## Off-the-shelf: aim to order by mid-December, preferably earlier

For off-the-shelf products, plan to have orders placed by mid-December at the latest if you are targeting delivery before the Christmas break. Earlier is better, especially for a larger order or a particular finish.

Treat that as our planning deadline, not a guarantee that every item ordered by then will arrive before Christmas. We will need to confirm stock, supplier acceptance, freight and installation availability for your order. Some products or delivery locations will need an earlier cut-off.

“Off-the-shelf” also needs checking. A product in a catalogue is not necessarily sitting in a warehouse waiting for your name on it.

Other businesses are trying to use the same quiet weeks. You may be competing for the same stock, freight capacity and installation dates. A quote is useful; confirmed availability and an agreed delivery program are what make the plan workable.

## A friendly nudge for the spicy-brain planning committee

If you describe yourself as having a spicy brain, live with ADHD, or simply have seventeen priorities open at once, consider this your friendly calendar nudge.

You do not need to arrive with the perfect brief. Start with three things: what is not working, when your team finishes for the year, and when everyone comes back.

If your brain has filed this under “future me will handle it”, this is future you calling. They would quite like a desk that arrives on time.

No judgement, no award for the most polished spreadsheet. Just one practical next step before “plenty of time” becomes “can we get it by Friday?”

## What could a Christmas workplace refresh include?

The right scope might be a few targeted changes rather than a complete transformation:

- Replace furniture that no longer suits the way your team works.
- Reconfigure workstations or storage around a measured layout.
- Refresh a reception area, meeting room or shared space.
- Coordinate agreed refurbishment works with the appropriate contractors.
- Arrange a scoped commercial clean after installation or works, before people return.

## Before you switch on the out-of-office

Agree the scope and budget, nominate one decision-maker, and confirm the site access and return-to-work date. Include landlord or building approvals where needed, IT coordination, delivery access, waste removal, final cleaning and a handover check.

A small, well-organised refresh can be a much better result than an ambitious project squeezed into a window it does not fit.
